concerns.text: T017 (split_half_validator) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but depends on T016 (glm_fitter) which produces the effect size estimates required for the split-half validation logic. The split-half validator cannot run in parallel with the GLM fitter as it consumes its output. The [P] tag is incorrect here.

T019 (error handling in split_half_validator) is marked [P] but depends on T017. Since T017 is a single execution step (not a loop) and T019 modifies the logic of T017 to handle iteration failures, T019 cannot be parallelized independently of T017's implementation state. The [P] tag is misleading.

T022 (power_curve_generator) is marked [P] but depends on T012-T017 (Core Implementation) and T008 (Data Fetcher). While T022 orchestrates the loop, the task description implies it runs the entire bootstrap loop. If T022 is a single task that runs 50 iterations, it is NOT parallel-safe. If it is meant to be a module that *can* be parallelized, the task description must explicitly state it delegates to a parallel runner (e.g., T041a). As written, it appears to be a monolithic execution step, making the [P] tag incorrect.

T024 (logistic regression) is marked [P] but depends on T022 (power curve generation) and T014 (noise estimator). The regression model requires the aggregated power curve data (output of T022) and the noise estimate (output of T014). It cannot run in parallel with T022 or T014. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T031b (temporal_sensitivity_orchestrator) is marked [P] but depends on T031 (parameter injection) and T022. It orchestrates the comparison loop. If T031b runs the loop, it is not parallel-safe. If it is a module, the dependency on T031 (which modifies T022) creates a tight coupling that prevents independent parallel execution of T031b without T031 being complete. The [P] tag is likely incorrect.

T018 (main.py entry point) is marked [P] but depends on T004-T009, T012-T017, T022, T029. It orchestrates the entire pipeline. It cannot run in parallel with any of its dependencies. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T038 (wall-clock time monitoring) is marked [P] but depends on T038b (timer implementation). T038 is the *usage* of the timer, while T038b is the *implementation*. T038 cannot run in parallel with T038b. The [P] tag is incorrect.
T055 (result_finalizer) is marked [P] but depends on T026, T032, T049, T050. It aggregates all final results. It cannot run in parallel with any of its dependencies. The [P] tag is incorrect.
T056 (validation script) is marked [P] but depends on T055 (final report). It validates the output of T055. It cannot run in parallel with T055. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T057 (alpha_sweep_runner) is marked [P] but depends on T022 and T029. It re-runs the power curve generation for different alpha values. This is a sequential re-run of T022, not a parallel task. The [P] tag is incorrect.
T058 (update final report) is marked [P] but depends on T057 and T055. It updates the report with alpha sweep results. It cannot run in parallel with T057 or T055. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T016 (GLM Fitter) depends on T013 (temporal smoothing). T013 depends on T012 (ROI extractor). T012 depends on T008 (Data Fetcher). The dependency chain is correct, but the task descriptions for T012, T013, and T016 do not explicitly mention the 'simulated sample size' (subsampling) logic required by US-1. This creates a semantic gap where the 'real data' input might not be subsampled before GLM fitting, violating the 'simulated sample size' requirement.

T031b (temporal_sensitivity_orchestrator) depends on T031 (parameter injection). T031 is described as 'parameter injection in power_curve_generator'. This implies T031 modifies T022. T031b then calls T022. The dependency is T031b -> T031 -> T022. However, T031 is marked [P] and T031b is marked [P]. If T031 modifies T022, T031b cannot run until T031 is complete. The [P] tags are inconsistent with the dependency chain.
